subject: Onramp reschedule + KV-cache / throughput thresholds for hands-on session
messages:
From: Alex Garner <alex@gameforge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Bethany Li <bethany.li@stellarai.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T16:12:00-05:00
Subject: Redwood onramp — hands-on session & load test windows

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the demo was helpful. We want to get the hands-on onramp scheduled next week so our infra and ML teams can validate routing and KV-cache behavior under load. Two quick asks before we lock a slot:

- Can you confirm what the test harness will do to warm the KV cache (unique prefixes, warm-up duration)?
- Our SREs want target throughput and latency SLOs so they can size a staging cluster.

We are available Tuesday or Thursday morning PT. Attaching a short doc with our suggested traffic mix.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Principal Engineer, GameForge

Attachments: gameforge_test_mix.csv (referenced)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garner <alex@gameforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T18:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onramp — hands-on session & load test windows

Alex — thanks, this is perfect context. Quick answers and a proposed plan:

- KV-cache warm-up: our harness can replay N unique prefixes to simulate cold prefixes and then run a warm-up pass of 1,000 unique prefixes over 10 minutes to establish a KV hit rate baseline. We will provide the exact script (kv_warmup_matrix.csv) and expect ~85% hit rate after warm-up for short-prefix reuse patterns.

- Throughput & latency SLOs: we typically validate with two target profiles:
  1) Interactive: 200 concurrent sessions, p95 latency < 350ms, p99 < 900ms (single-token step for streaming enabled).
  2) Batch/Throughput: 1,000 concurrent short requests (avg 60 tokens), sustained for 10 minutes; tail p99 < 1.2s.

Proposed slots (PT): Tue 2026-11-10 09:00–12:00 or Thu 2026-11-12 09:00–12:00. We will run the warm-up then three stepped load runs (light → peak → soak).

I've attached our internal test plan and an .ics with both slots. If you prefer a different cadence, we can shorten to a 2-hour focused throughput window.

Next steps: pick a slot and confirm attendee list (SRE + ML + product).

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: inference_test_plan.pdf, proposed_calendar_slots.ics

Our SRE lead (on the thread) prefers two separate blocks: one for integration + prompt review, one for the heavy load so they can bring extra nodes for the soak.

Two proposed blocks (PT):
- Tue 2026-11-10 09:30–11:00 — integration, prompt review, KV-warm-up
- Fri 2026-11-13 08:00–10:30 — throughput soak (we'll provision staging nodes)

Can you confirm Redwood can split the work across two sessions and provide the exact warm-up script so our SREs can pre-seed data? Also, if you have any hard time windows (maintenance), flag them now.

Alex

Alex — that works fine. We'll split into the two blocks you suggested. Quick logistics and checklist before we lock calendar invites: 

1) Tue 2026-11-10 09:30–11:00 PT — Integration, prompt review, KV warm-up (attendees: Alex, Bethany, GF SRE lead, Priyom, Marissa). Deliverables: warm-up script (kv_warmup_matrix.csv), sample prompts, low-latency profile run.

2) Fri 2026-11-13 08:00–10:30 PT — Throughput soak (attendees: GF SRE, Redwood infra ops, Karthik). Deliverables: three stepped runs (light/peak/soak), rps/tokens/time traces, and post-run p95/p99 report.

Notes: 
- We'll share the warm-up script by EOD (kv_warmup_matrix.csv). Please confirm any CIDR rules we should add for the staging nodes.
- Target numbers we'll validate against during the soak: peak concurrent ~1,000 short requests (avg 60 tokens), expected sustained token throughput ~4k–6k tokens/sec, p95 < 450ms, p99 < 1.2s. If you need tighter tail latency, flag now so we can change instance sizing.

I've attached the test plan and the warm-up CSV. I'll send calendar invites once you confirm attendees and CIDRs.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
